source.name: sp_GetOrderShippingInfo
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo
    @OrderID INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        m.MetadataXml.value('(/order/shipping/address)[1]', 'NVARCHAR(500)') AS ShippingAddress,
        m.MetadataXml.value('(/order/shipping/method)[1]', 'NVARCHAR(100)') AS ShippingMethod,
        m.MetadataXml.query('/order/items') AS ItemsXml
    FROM dbo.Orders o
    INNER JOIN dbo.OrderMetadata m ON o.OrderID = m.OrderID
    WHERE o.OrderID = @OrderID;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo(
    p_OrderID INTEGER
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    OrderID INTEGER,
    ShippingAddress VARCHAR(500),
    ShippingMethod VARCHAR(100),
    ItemsXml XML
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        (xpath('/order/shipping/address/text()', m.MetadataXml))[1]::TEXT::VARCHAR(500) AS ShippingAddress,
        (xpath('/order/shipping/method/text()', m.MetadataXml))[1]::TEXT::VARCHAR(100) AS ShippingMethod,
        (xpath('/order/items', m.MetadataXml))[1] AS ItemsXml
    FROM dbo.Orders o
    INNER JOIN dbo.OrderMetadata m ON o.OrderID = m.OrderID
    WHERE o.OrderID = p_OrderID;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The MetadataXml column in OrderMetadata table is of type XML in PostgreSQL
The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL database
SQL Server's .value() method maps to PostgreSQL's xpath() function with array indexing
SQL Server's .query() method maps to PostgreSQL's xpath() function
XPath expressions return text nodes that need to be cast to TEXT then to VARCHAR
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row counts by default in functions)
Parameter name prefixed with p_ to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions and avoid conflicts

reviewFlags.reason: XPath conversion from SQL Server's .value() method requires careful testing. The xpath() function returns an array, and [1] gets the first element. Verify that the XPath expressions produce the expected results and handle NULL cases appropriately.

SQL Server's .query() method returns XML fragments. PostgreSQL's xpath() returns an XML array. Verify that returning the first element [1] produces the desired XML structure. May need xmlelement() or other XML functions for exact compatibility.
Ensure the MetadataXml column is defined as XML type in PostgreSQL. If it's stored as TEXT, additional casting with ::XML will be required.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's XQuery methods (.value(), .query()) have different syntax than PostgreSQL's xpath() function. PostgreSQL xpath() returns arrays of XML nodes, requiring array indexing and explicit casting.
Converted from PROCEDURE to FUNCTION returning TABLE. Callers must use SELECT * FROM dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo(order_id) instead of EXEC dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo @OrderID = order_id.
If XPath expressions don't match any nodes, PostgreSQL returns an empty array. Accessing [1] on an empty array returns NULL, which should match SQL Server behavior when .value() finds no match.
PostgreSQL functions don't send row count messages by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON behavior is implicit and the statement is omitted.
